item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1550

Shortcuts

  • Preferences > Shortcuts: every action with Kento's key and yours, found by name or by pressing its keys. Click a key cap and press the new keys; a conflict shows as you press. Your set can be exported and imported, and the full keyboard shows what every key does, with the modifiers held.
  • Tooltips, menu rows and chips that name a key show your key, and follow when you change it. Help > Keyboard shortcuts lists your keys.

3D scenes out

  • WriteGeo: the comp's 3D written to one Alembic or USD file (.abc, .usd, .usda, .usdc). Cameras from the CameraTracker or Export > Camera move every frame; cards, spheres, cubes, cylinders, ReadGeo2 meshes and imported scenes go where Nuke's own WriteGeo puts them.
  • Its panel: the file type, what to write, the range on one row with limit to range, and Write file, which writes in the background and says what it wrote.
  • The Render window and queue list a WriteGeo as one job over its whole range; command-line renders write WriteGeos too, once each.

Projection

  • Projecting onto heavy meshes is about a hundred times faster: an HD frame onto 200,000 triangles in under a second.
  • Paint as: in a wide-gamut comp, choose the painting's file (a 16-bit sRGB TIFF, a 16-bit TIFF with ACEScg primaries that clips nothing, or the linear EXR). Preferences > General > Paint sets the default.
  • Pad for paint: the percentage of the whole canvas or on each side; extend edges is the default fill; the edges line speaks of the padded canvas.

Deep

  • DeepReformat's flip, flop, turn and center; resize none; box_fixed off keeps the input's shape. Samples move whole, never resampled.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1527

Projection

  • Project this frame: Option-P over the Viewer, or the Viewer menu's Projection section. Builds a Projection at the current frame from the Viewer's picture and the comp's tracked camera, in one undo.
  • The Projection node: one tile that opens (Cmd+Return) to ordinary nodes: held camera, held image, projector, card or geometry, render through the shot camera over the plate. A Nuke script gets a Group of the same nodes.
  • One hold frame, shown on the tile, as a diamond on the timeline and as a badge in the Viewer; Go to hold and Hold here. The held camera follows the track; Bake held camera freezes a copy.
  • Onto: a card at a depth (typed, or clicked in the Viewer from the plate's depth or the nearest tracked point), a card through selected tracked points, or selected geometry.
  • Edges: black outside the image or extended edges, with where the card leaves the image and an overscan button.
  • Pad for paint: a larger canvas to paint past the plate's edges, optionally upscaled, projected so the original pixels stay where they were.
  • Send to paint: the held frame written out and opened in your paint app (Preferences > General > Paint); saving there updates the projection. New version, Back to plate, a round-trip test, and checks when the painting comes back.
  • Coverage in the Viewer: where the projection falls outside the held image, faces away, is hidden or grazes, on the shot itself, with the worst frames marked along the timeline.
  • Front faces only and occlusion are drawn as Nuke draws them.
  • Scripts whose image and camera holds disagree say so, with a choice to line them up or keep them.

3D for projection

  • BlendMat and MergeMat, to stack projections; UVProject, DisplaceGeo, ApplyMaterial, ModelBuilder, Reconcile3D and ScanlineRender2.
  • Nuke's USD-based GeoCard, GeoImport, GeoReference, GeoBindMaterial, GeoScene and GeoViewScene. File > Import > USD scene... and dropping a .usd on the graph make a GeoImport.
  • ScanlineRender's ambient.

Deep

  • DeepMerge2's plus; DeepCrop's outside z range and outside box.

Node Graph and panels

  • A node's label shows under its tile.
  • MultiMerge's layer list: the drag grips show, and the list follows new layers.
  • The older SphericalTransform's face forward switch is shown, with what it does.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1472

New nodes

  • MultiMerge's layer list: top layer first, drag to reorder, each layer's eye, solo, operation and mix.
  • LayerMux (Channel): several pictures into one multi-layer picture, each input a layer of its own.
  • PickMatte (Keyer): a matte grown from a picked pixel by color tolerance and softness.
  • DepthToPosition (3D): each pixel's world position from its depth and the camera.
  • Axis4 and Cylinder (3D). Cylinder renders as NukeX does.
  • Lights and shaders (3D): Light2, Light3, DirectLight, PointLight and Spotlight; Phong, Diffuse, Specular, Emission and BasicMaterial. Lit cards match NukeX.
  • The older SphericalTransform class: its seven projections, rotations on both sides, and fix.
  • VariableSwitch, VectorToMotion, Encryptomatte, Profile, ScannedGrain, Sparkles, BumpBoss, DegrainSimple, LevelSet, VectorCornerPin, SphericalTransform2 and TVIscale2.

Finished

  • DeepColorCorrect2: contrast, the shadows, midtones and highlights rows, mix, and the depth range. Several samples a pixel are corrected as NukeX does.
  • GridWarp3's morph mix.
  • FrameRepair can make bad frames from the motion around them, and TemporalSmooth can follow motion.
  • Reformat's input and output crops, and "to size".

Panels: controls in place of typing

  • Curves you draw: ScannedGrain's weight, ColorLookup, HueCorrect, HueKeyer, AddMix, CCrosstalk, TimeDissolve and ColorCorrect's ranges have a graph above their text. Click to add a key and drag to move it. Right-click to delete it, set it smooth, linear or a step, or reset the curve. Hue curves have a strip of the hues under them.
  • Matrix: the kernel as a grid of fields, with a size menu and starting kernels (blur, sharpen, edge, emboss).
  • Text's font: a family menu and a style menu, filled from the Mac's fonts.
  • ModifyMetaData: its edits as a table, with the input's keys to pick.
  • LayerFilter: the input's layers to tick. VariableSwitch: the variable's values to tick for each input. LayerMux's layer names come from a menu.
  • View knobs (Anaglyph, MixViews, JoinViews, Write) are menus and check boxes. OCIOLookTransform's look is a menu. Write's EXR compression is a menu.
  • Bezier: Convert to Roto, to edit its points in the Viewer.
  • Every menu knob is now a menu, filled with its items.
  • The mask strip appears on every node that has a mask.

Other

  • The Pixel inspector (Window > Panels): pin points and boxes, read live, with min, max, mean and median.
  • Viewer > Zebra: stripes over pixels at or above a level.
  • How a node reaches a Nuke script: a node that will be baked on export has a film mark on its tile, and the panel's first line says so. PickMatte is now offered for baking.
